title: Choosing a perturbation subset for non-polynomial functions
summary: Modifying a polynomial can yield a non-polynomial function, but choosing a subset that avoids polynomial closeness without excessive implementation cost remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Given a polynomial function $P$ over $\mathbb{Z}_{p^n}$, determine how to choose a subset of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^n}$ on which to modify $P$ so that the resulting function $F$ is non-polynomial, is not too close to a polynomial function, and remains practical to implement. The unresolved tradeoff is that perturbing too small a subset leaves $F$ too close to being polynomial, whereas perturbing a large subset may make $F$ expensive to implement.

scope.domain: Cryptographic design of non-polynomial functions over integer rings.
parameters: P, the polynomial function over the integer ring
A subset of the integer ring, the points on which P is modified
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine how to choose the subset so that the resulting function F is not too close to a polynomial function while remaining practical to implement.

citations.label: The ABC of Symmetric Primitives over Integer Rings: Milk Before Meat

progress.summary: The source explicitly frames the choice of the perturbation subset as a problem after observing that perturbing a polynomial yields a non-polynomial function. It leaves unresolved the tradeoff between polynomial closeness for a small subset and implementation cost for a large subset.
